prompt:
Image 1 is a pixel-art sprite sheet of the upper body of a small chibi knight for a top-down 2D game, holding a sword in the right hand and a blue shield in the left hand. Create ONE NEW sheet of the same upper body doing one fast flat horizontal sword slash in four frames. The blade sweeps a half circle around the knight, level with the ground, from the knight's right side, through the front, to the knight's left side. Keep exactly the same character, armour, helmet, size, proportions, palette, sword, shield and pixel-art style, on the same flat solid pure magenta background, RGB 255,0,255.

Upper body only: the helmet, head, shoulders, torso, both arms, the sword and the shield, stopping at the belt. There is no skirt, no legs and no feet.

Layout: exactly 3 rows and 4 columns, one upper body per cell, with clear magenta space around each one so that nothing touches.

The most important rule: within a row, only the sword arm and the sword move. The helmet, the head, the torso, the shield arm and the shield are identical in all four columns of that row, in exactly the same place. The shield never changes sides and never moves.
In row 1 the shield is always on the right side of the picture.
In row 2 the shield is always at the front of the body, on the right side of the picture.
In row 3 the shield is always on the left side of the picture.

Row 1: seen from the front, facing the viewer. The sword is in the hand on the left side of the picture.
Column 1: the sword arm is stretched out to the left of the picture at shoulder height, and the blade points straight to the left.
Column 2: the sword arm reaches forward and down on the left side of the picture, and the blade points to the lower left.
Column 3: the sword arm reaches forward across the belt, and the blade points to the lower right.
Column 4: the sword arm has swung across the chest, the hand in front of the shield, and the blade points straight to the right, passing in front of the shield.

Row 2: seen from the side, facing right. The sword is in the arm nearest to the viewer.
Column 1: the sword arm is held down by the hip, and the blade points straight down.
Column 2: the sword arm reaches forward and low, and the blade points down and to the right.
Column 3: the sword arm is stretched forward at chest height, and the blade points up and to the right.
Column 4: the sword arm has swung up in front of the chest, the hand in front of the shoulder, and the blade points straight up.

Row 3: seen from the back, facing away from the viewer. The sword is in the hand on the right side of the picture.
Column 1: the sword arm is stretched out to the right of the picture at shoulder height, and the blade points straight to the right.
Column 2: the sword arm reaches forward and up on the right side of the picture, and the blade points to the upper right.
Column 3: the sword arm reaches up beside the helmet, and the blade points to the upper left, passing behind the helmet.
Column 4: the sword arm has swung across behind the helmet, and the blade points straight to the left.

In every frame the fingers are tightly closed around the sword's handle and the blade is a straight extension of the hand, so that the arm and the sword move together as one piece. The sword must be fully visible and must not be cut off.

Do not include: legs, feet, a skirt, text, labels, numbers, grid lines, ground, shadows, dust, motion lines, slash effects, borders, watermark, or any other object. No soft gradients, blur or painterly rendering.
